intro: STL to OBJ converts 3D models from STL to OBJ on the server, with nothing to install. It is useful, for example, to take a part downloaded from Printables or Thingiverse into Blender or a viewer to edit or render it. OBJ is the exchange format of Blender, Maya, 3ds Max and almost every viewer: it stores several named parts and, with its MTL file, materials and colours.

STL is the format every slicer reads (PrusaSlicer, Cura, Bambu Studio, OrcaSlicer): it only stores triangles, with no units or colours, as text (ASCII) or binary. STL does not store units and is taken as millimetres, the usual case; if your model was drawn in centimetres, metres or inches, say so and the conversion turns it into the units you want for the OBJ. You can also apply a scale, for example 0.5 to print the STL at half size.

If the model has colours, the OBJ comes in a ZIP with its MTL file, one material per colour, so Blender or the viewer shows them. If the STL has several parts, you can keep them separate inside the OBJ when the format allows it, merge them into one mesh or get one file per part in a ZIP.

The geometry is not simplified or repaired: every triangle of the STL reaches the OBJ unchanged, with duplicate vertices merged. Up to one million triangles are accepted without an account, two million with a free account and ten million with Pro, checked before the file is processed. Files are deleted automatically when they expire.
steps: Upload one or more STL files.
Choose the units and, optionally, the scale and parts.

faq.q: Why does my STL come out tiny or huge?
faq.a: Because the target program assumes other units. Set the units of the original and of the OBJ.
No: the OBJ has exactly the same geometry. To close holes or fix normals, use Repair STL.
